subject.title: Design: Telegram isolated ingress holds per-chat lane for the entire agent turn — long turns block the group, then die at 25 min

question: Should Telegram isolated polling release a per-chat/topic spool lane after durable session-admission handoff instead of keeping it active until the full agent turn settles?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the permanent fix changes Telegram transport ordering, duplicate/replay safety, timeout semantics, and session-admission ownership, which needs maintainer intent before automation edits code.

options.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
options.body: Move the spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

options.title: Keep Transport Lane Ownership
options.body: Preserve one active handler per lane and only tune timeout, recovery, or progress feedback, accepting that same-lane messages still cannot reach admission during a long turn.

options.title: Split Narrow Follow-Ups
options.body: Track handler-timeout visibility, timeout recovery, progress feedback, and claude-cli live injection separately while keeping this issue as the lane-ownership design item.

recommendation.title: Detach After Durable Handoff
recommendation.body: Move the spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to this issue and have the strongest recent history across the Telegram spool and related run-lifecycle surfaces.
